title: RTK Query Modern APIs and Version Traps Checkpoint

questions.prompt: An infinite feed varies by tenant and topic and navigates using a cursor. How should it be modeled?

options.label: Tenant/topic in queryArg; cursor in pageParam.
Only the cursor in queryArg; tenant/topic are never cache dimensions.
A new API slice for every fetched page.

questions.explanation: The collection identity stays stable across pages while the page parameter advances. Dropping tenant/topic creates collisions, and per-page API slices fragment subscriptions and invalidation.

questions.prompt: Which version first added Standard Schema validation to RTK Query?

options.label: RTK 2.12.0 was the first version with any endpoint schemas.

questions.explanation: Standard Schema support arrived in 2.7.0. The case-study 2.2.8 baseline predates it; 2.12.0 includes later fixes and improvements rather than introducing the original schema API.

questions.prompt: In RTK 2.11+, what does refetchCachedPages: false do on an infinite-query refetch?

options.label: Disables every future request for this endpoint.
Refetches the first cached page and shrinks the retained cache to one page.
Refreshes the first page and keeps all remaining cached pages unchanged.

questions.explanation: The option collapses the retained window to one refreshed page. It does not preserve all later pages and does not disable the endpoint; scroll behavior needs an explicit product policy.

questions.prompt: Schema validation fails and normal endpoint error behavior is desired. What converts the failure?

options.label: catchSchemaFailure returning the base query error shape.
onSchemaFailure alone always converts it into a handled error.
A TypeScript assertion on the response payload.

questions.explanation: catchSchemaFailure performs conversion. onSchemaFailure is a notification hook; casting a payload neither validates it nor changes the runtime error path.

questions.prompt: How should the modern cancellation behavior be described?

options.label: Every component unmount immediately cancels every shared request.
Aborting a request guarantees the server transaction was rolled back.
Cache-entry removal can abort pending work; one subscriber unmount is not always removal.

questions.explanation: Modern RTK ties automatic abort to entry removal. Shared subscriptions and retention can keep work alive; even a transport abort cannot prove rollback of a remote write.

questions.prompt: A response is transformed before caching. Which schema validates the wire shape first?

options.label: skipSchemaValidation validates the raw shape more strictly.
responseSchema always validates only the original wire shape.

questions.explanation: rawResponseSchema validates before transformResponse; responseSchema validates the final result. skipSchemaValidation disables checks and is not a stricter validation mode.
